# CrypTool legacy homophonic-100 finite result (ASTRA)

The registered scan completed once and retained every one of the 64,000 plaintext candidates. It covered four hexadecimal orientations, four decimal orientations, 40 multipliers coprime to 100, and 100 rotations. All 16 representation paths produced 1,316 decimal digits and 658 decoded letters after one parity zero was restored. Every stored row passed exact code-to-letter membership and whole-integer reconstruction.

No candidate in the global top ten reads as coherent English. This is a manual observation over the retained highest-ranked rows, not a heuristic exclusion. The best score was `-12.97678599630823`; the synthetic random control scored `-13.035030368909128`, while the held-out English controls scored `-12.818391670638409` and `-12.794345956477203`. This small sibling-trained model only orders candidates.

## Evidence and reproduction

- Immutable gate SHA-256: `7e4abe97633b97442ff8a6c807e5efd6fa80c4416717594847e7f8bff3cfb448`.
- Frozen driver SHA-256: `e76c3da624a5fef003ca8853fa3466d826c7afaf143f3606810ca2e3ee8013e0`.
- Complete NDJSON: 67,783,676 bytes, SHA-256 `426a5be079cf553ba657e3bb3f9d4e8153ee15422efc0e8793e1840249dcac39`; 1 header plus 64,000 candidate rows.
- Summary JSON SHA-256: `a1f04beb731abc2d3f4c9557bb82fa345e6ebf128599f66e33e07b08b8e9beec`.
- The lossless Base85/zlib envelope reconstructs the exact NDJSON bytes. Its decoder bounds output to the registered raw length, requires one complete stream with no tail, and checks raw/compressed hashes.
- The portable verifier checks the source and gate pins, canonical MDX/dataset agreement, all 64,000 Cartesian IDs, independent historical board decoding, plaintext hashes, exact flags, and stored top-20 ordering. It does not perform a second target enumeration.

From the repository root:

```sh
python3 -S -B research/rev7-20260909-codex/homophonic/cryptool100/target/pack_results.py
python3 -S -B research/rev7-20260909-codex/homophonic/cryptool100/target/verify_results.py
```

The finite result applies only to the exact historical German allocation, affine board family, whole-integer conversion, and registered representation orientations. Additional lost `00` pairs may encode an unknown plaintext prefix or suffix. Rankings do not exclude low-scoring candidates and do not cover other homophonic boards, encodings, transcription changes, or chained ciphers.
